---
title: "strsplit() reads the separator as a regular expression"
ref: STR-01
categories: [Strings]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'strsplit("a.b", ".")[[1]]'
reponse: '"" "" ""'
attendu: "`\"a\" \"b\"`"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
strsplit("a.b", split = ".")
strsplit("2026.10.23", split = ".")
strsplit("a|b", split = "|")
```
:::

## Why

The `split` argument is a regular expression, and in a regular expression the dot means "any character". Every character of the string is therefore a separator, and only empty pieces are left between them.

The vertical bar `|` means "or": `"|"` is the alternation between two empty patterns, which matches the empty string. `strsplit()` then splits between every character, and the bar ends up in the result instead of disappearing.

## The remedy

Ask for a literal match with `fixed = TRUE`, or escape the special character.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
strsplit("a.b", split = ".", fixed = TRUE)
strsplit("a|b", split = "\\|")
```
:::
